paragraphs.text: Pontotoc County is under an outdoor burn ban beginning Tuesday, Oct. 20, with Nov. 20 listed as its end date by the Mississippi Forestry Commission. The Town of Ecru also alerted residents to the ban Tuesday afternoon.

The commission’s general guidance prohibits campfires, bonfires, fire pits, fire rings, burn barrels, debris burning and field burning during a burn ban. It describes the restriction as covering open flames that produce embers.

Pontotoc’s listing includes exemptions 1, 2 and 4. Those cover the Forestry Commission, certified burn managers and construction contractors using heavy equipment, provided the contractors’ burns meet Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality regulations.

The state guidance lists gas or propane grills and heaters, along with charcoal grills, as allowed. It calls for following manufacturer instructions, keeping them away from combustible materials and never leaving them unattended. Charcoal should cool completely and be doused with water before disposal in a metal container.

The local restriction follows a Tuesday morning National Weather Service outlook warning of continued afternoon fire danger across the Mid-South. Residents should check the commission’s live county listing, linked below, for current dates and exemptions before planning any outdoor burning.
